Kamlager-Dove Statement on the Massie Amendment | Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove Skip to main content 144 Cannon House Office Building, Washington DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-7084 Kamlager-Dove Statement on the Massie Amendment July 15, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C.  — Today, Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37)  released the following statement on Massie Amendment 8, which blocks U.S. military assistance to Israel in the 2027 National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act. In this bill, 98.5% of the funding appropriated for Israel is designated for F oreign Military Financing.   "When I signed onto the Block the Bombs Act, I committed  to opposing offensive military aid to the Netanyahu government while still supporting funding for defensive programs. That's why, after receiving assurances that funding for the Iron Dome would be unaffected, I voted to block taxpayer funding to Israel in the 2027 National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act.    "Key to my vote was the elimination of $3.3 billion in Foreign Military Financing to Israel. Over the years, Prime Minister Netanyahu has repeatedly used U.S. military assistance to commit gross violations of human rights, prolong conflict, and retain his hold on power. I cannot in good conscience support using U.S. taxpayer dollars to help finance Netanyahu's war apparatus.”   ###

Kamlager-Dove Celebrates the GRATEFUL Act Being Signed Into Law | Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove Skip to main content 144 Cannon House Office Building, Washington DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-7084 Kamlager-Dove Celebrates the GRATEFUL Act Being Signed Into Law December 22, 2023 Press Release FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE -  December 22, 2023 Media Contact:   Maya Valentine |   maya.valentine@mail.house.gov WASHINGTON, DC – Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37) issued the following statement after President Biden signed the GRATEFUL Act into law, which Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove introduced in the House with Congresswoman Maria Salazar (FL-27).  “I am thrilled to see President Biden sign the bipartisan Granting Recognition to Accomplished Talented Employees for Unwavering Loyalty (GRATEFUL) Act into law today as part of the Fiscal Year 2024 National Defense Authorization Act package. This bill, which I introduced in the House, was a top legislative priority for the State Department this year. Even in the midst of unprecedented Republican dysfunction, I was able to work with my colleagues in the Senate and at the State Department as a first-term Member in my first year in office to ensure this bill was signed into law.  "The GRATEFUL Act provides visas for locally employed U.S. embassy staff to immigrate to the U.S. after a career of service to the United States. It allows us to keep our promise to these individuals who have earned and deserve the opportunity to pursue a better life for themselves and their families in the U.S. Importantly, the embassy staff who will benefit from this provision come from countries in the Global South and other hot spots, where they work in often dangerous conditions on behalf of the United States. Currently, over 2,000 people who have spent their careers serving the United States abroad are waiting for visas that will be freed up as a result of the GRATEFUL Act. "I came to Congress to advance meaningful policy initiatives and am glad to have my first bill signed into law. I would like to thank Congresswoman Salazar and Senators Van Hollen and Tillis for their support of this critical legislation.” # # #

Kamlager-Dove Statement on Republicans’ America Last Budget | Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove Skip to main content 144 Cannon House Office Building, Washington DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-7084 Kamlager-Dove Statement on Republicans’ America Last Budget July 22, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C.  — Today, Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37)  released the following statement after voting against the budget framework for a third reconciliation package: “Gas is still $6 per gallon in California. The cost of groceries continues to rise. Eight million Americans have lost health care because of Republican cuts. An estimated $100 billion has already been spent on Trump’s war of choice with Iran. Now Republicans want to give Trump and Hegseth more money for a botched war that is making life more expensive? It’s a hell no from me. “Republicans insist this funding is necessary to keep the Pentagon afloat, but they created this mess by allowing small men with fragile egos to drag us into a conflict with no strategic endgame. We are now fighting to reopen a strait that was open before the war began. This is madness. Instead of asking for more money, the administration must get serious about negotiating a way out and preventing further harm to our servicemembers. “Americans do not want to see their tax dollars thrown at another endless war, they want to see them invested back into their pockets and communities. This America Last budget once again proves how out-of-touch Republicans are with the needs of their constituents. Democrats will keep fighting to bring down costs and make life easier for hard-working families.” # # #

Kamlager-Dove Announces Bill to Ensure Medical Care for ICE Detainees | Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove Skip to main content 144 Cannon House Office Building, Washington DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-7084 Kamlager-Dove Announces Bill to Ensure Medical Care for ICE Detainees July 29, 2026 Press Release LOS ANGELES, CA – Today,  Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37)  held a press conference to announce the upcoming introduction of her Stop ICE’s Medical Neglect Act of 2026, legislation that creates a standardized system to report medical neglect in ICE detention facilities, requires each complaint to be investigated, and ensures adequate follow-up care. The congresswoman was joined by Reps. Judy Chu (CA-28) , Lou Correa (CA-46) , and  Gil Cisneros (CA-31) . A livestream is available here . This legislation is in direct response to ICE repeatedly denying proper medical care  to Carlitos Ricardo Parias, a constituent of Rep. Kamlager-Dove, following a gunshot wound  he suffered during an immigration enforcement traffic stop in October. He has been detained at Adelanto since December. “Our humanity does not end at the doors of an ICE detention center. No one should suffer in government custody because their medical needs were ignored,” said Rep. Kamlager-Dove . “Yet for nearly a year, my constituent Ricardo has repeatedly sought medical care at Adelanto, only to watch his pleas go unanswered and his condition worsen. Tragically, Ricardo’s story is not unique. That’s why I’m introducing the Stop ICE’s Medical Neglect Act to track these instances of abuse and ensure every detainee receives the timely and appropriate care they deserve.” "We will not stand by while our immigrant neighbors are abused, denied basic human dignity, and treated as though their lives do not matter," said Rep. Judy Chu . "Rep. Kamlager-Dove’s legislation is so important because it will provide permanent protections for detainees by allowing them and their advocates to report medical neglect, and ensure those complaints are reviewed by board-certified medical professionals. Those responsible for the suffering and deaths in U.S. custody must be held accountable.”  "Nobo

Kamlager-Dove Demands Proper Medical Care for Constituent Detained by ICE | Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove Skip to main content 144 Cannon House Office Building, Washington DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-7084 Kamlager-Dove Demands Proper Medical Care for Constituent Detained by ICE July 23, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today on the House Floor, Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37) once again demanded that ICE provide proper medical care to her constituent, Carlitos Ricardo Parias. Parias suffered a gunshot wound during an immigration enforcement operation last October. Since being detained at the Adelanto ICE Processing Center, Parias has been denied proper care to address lingering health issues stemming from his gunshot wound. In late May, Rep. Kamlager-Dove conducted an oversight visit at Adelanto, where she met with Parias and obtained his medical records . Last week, following advocacy from Rep. Kamlager-Dove and others, a federal judge ordered sweeping changes to improve conditions for detainees at Adelanto. Image You can watch her remarks  here or read them below: "Mr. Speaker, I rise today to once again demand that ICE immediately provide my constituent, Carlitos Ricardo Parias, urgently needed medical care. Carlitos is a father. A husband. A volunteer in our community who was even recognized by City Council for his service. "Last October, ICE shot Carlitos near his elbow. He received initial care at a hospital. But since being transferred to the Adelanto ICE facility in December, ICE has denied him proper care for the injury they caused. "I visited Carlitos in late May. His hand was purple. His fingers were atrophied. He’s experiencing headaches and nerve pain. I’m worried that he may have a bone infection and that his arm could be amputated. "Carlitos urgently needs medical attention—and many more at Adelanto do too.  Last week, a federal judge ordered sweeping changes to improve Adelanto’s conditions for detainees. It’s time for ICE to comply with this judge’s orders and end this cruelty—at Adelanto and nationwide. With that, I yield back."  # # #
